texts.full_text: pulse of a key measure of our water planet: how freshwater cycles over Earth's land surfaces in the form of soil moisture. The mission will produce the most accurate, highest-resolution global maps ever obtained from space of the moisture present in the top layer of soils across the globe. These detailed measurements are crucial for understanding and predicting weather patterns, as well as assessing drought conditions and managing agricultural resources more effectively. By providing data on soil moisture levels with unprecedented accuracy, SMAP will help improve climate models and contribute to better decision-making in areas such as water resource management, flood forecasting, and crop yield predictions. The satellite combines both active radar (which sends signals that bounce off the Earth's surface) and passive radiometry techniques (measuring natural microwave emissions from soil). This dual approach allows SMAP to gather data even under cloudy conditions or when vegetation covers much of the ground. The mission is expected to operate for at least three years, during which it will continuously monitor changes in global water distribution. NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laborator

texts.full_text: hlman Edward Bushrod Stahlman (September 2, 1843 – August 12, 1930) was a German-born American railroad executive, newspaper publisher and real estate investor. He was the vice president of the Louisville and Nashville Railroad and the Louisville, New Albany and Chicago Railroad. He built The Stahlman, a skyscraper in Nashville, Tennessee, and he was the publisher of the Nashville Banner for 44 years. Early life Edward Bushroad Stahlman was born as Friedrick Heinrich Eduard Stahlmann on September 2, 1843 in Güstrow, Germany. In, Stahlman and his family emigrated to the United States, settling in West Union, West Virginia. He had seven siblings. One of his sisters married Marcus B. Toney, a Klansman and Masonic leader. Career During the American Civil War, Edward Bushrod Stahlman served as an officer in the Confederate Army. After the war, he pursued various business ventures that contributed to his success in multiple industries. In the railroad sector, Stahlman became notably influential as the vice president of both the Louisville and Nashville Railroad and the Louisville, New Albany and Chicago Railroad. His leadership helped expand and modernize these rail networks, facilitating greater connectivity across several states. Stahlman's foray into real estate was marked by his construction of The Stahlman building in Nashville, Tennessee. Completed in 1898, this skyscraper stood as a testament to his vision and business acumen, becoming one of the tallest buildings in the city at that time. In addition to his ventures in railroads and real estate, Stahlman had a significant impact on the media industry through his role as the publisher of the Nashville Banner.
